channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Cameroon joins the list of African countries looking to Dangote for refining assistance
item.description: Sonara, a state-owned oil refinery in Cameroon, recently initiated a dialogue with Nigeria's Dangote Group in an effort to find funding and supply options for the long-delayed restart of its operations, which have been halted since a massive fire in 2019.

item.title: China offers South Africa duty-free market access amid pressure from US tariffs
item.description: China will allow duty-free imports of selected products from South Africa under a trade agreement currently being finalised, signalling Pretoria’s accelerating pivot toward alternative global markets as relations with the United States remain strained.

item.title: US threatens Africa’s second-most powerful military with sanctions over Russian Su-57 fighter jets deal
item.description: The United States has warned it may impose sanctions on Algeria over its decision to purchase advanced Russian-made Su-57 fighter jets, raising fresh questions about Africa’s defence ties with Moscow amid heightened global geopolitical tensions.

item.title: Africa’s richest country backs rare earths project with $20 million as EU seeks China alternatives
item.description: South Africa’s development finance institution has committed $20 million to a domestic rare earths project aimed at helping the European Union reduce its reliance on China for critical minerals.

item.title: As global powers race for Africa’s minerals, more nations are clamping down on raw mineral exports
item.description: From lithium and cobalt to gold, chrome, and uranium, African nations are shifting away from decades of raw mineral exports, which left processing, pricing power, and profits largely in foreign hands.

item.title: Global oil giant, Petrobras makes African comeback with new offshore oil acquisition
item.description: Brazil’s state-run oil major Petrobras is marking a strategic return to Africa with a 42.5% stake in an offshore oil exploration block off Namibia.

item.title: President Mahama sets $20bn-plus reserve goal to shield Ghana from external shocks
item.description: Ghana has set an ambitious target to grow its foreign exchange reserves beyond $20 billion by 2029, a move President John Dramani Mahama says is central to restoring macroeconomic stability and strengthening resilience against global shocks.

item.title: Top 10 deepest capital markets in Africa right now
item.description: Market depth, which is determined by the size and liquidity of domestic equity and bond markets, the variety of listed assets, and the presence of standard features that boost market participation, is more important than ever as African economies navigate a rapidly shifting global financial landscape in 2026.

item.title: Turkey signs $350 million arms deal with Africa’s most powerful military
item.description: Turkey has signed a $350 million defence agreement with Egypt, Africa’s top-ranked military and the world’s 19th strongest, highlighting Cairo’s expanding defence ambitions and Ankara’s deepening strategic push into African security markets.

item.title: After UK Home Office threats, 3 African countries agree deportation deal to take back migrants
item.description: Three African countries which include Angola, Namibia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have agreed to deportation deals to take back foreign offenders and illegal migrants from the United Kingdom following threats of visa penalties.
